focus: Widen to the corpus: how Figma's own skills, Adobe and community FigJam builders decide they know enough to act before drawing
noveltyJustification: Ten corpus findings, four genuinely new to this topic (project-plan rounds, per-section readiness, batched questions, stored answers) and six deepening iteration 1 gaps.
ruledOut: Copying approved_sections as a literal mechanism
Treating the four-questions-per-call limit as the round cap

label: Figma's own diagram skill carries the same one-or-two-question doctrine the packet quotes, so a multi-round intake has to exceed upstream rather than match it.
Figma's project-plan skill is the corpus's one real multi-round intake, modelling rounds as typed Research, Confirm and Write steps whose self-check may loop back and ask.
Its confidence test is a per-section readiness state - ready or a specific non-empty gap list of answerable facts - not a numeric score.
It caps the width of a round at four questions per call but never caps the number of rounds, which is the failure a round cap has to prevent.
It proposes rather than only asks: each card names a title, description, why it was suggested and a default shape, then content is previewed and answered Yes, Edit or Skip.
Answers persist as a named approved set with explicit skips, and an edited item is re-shown and re-asked, so later turns build on recorded state.

A machine-readable board plan already exists as precedent, with a purpose field defined as the question the diagram answers, notes for omissions and a skipped array with reasons; the packet lacks the purpose field.
The asking that exists upstream is scope-bounding or preference-settling, never comprehension-building about what the board must convince its reader of.
The only upstream cap is on regenerating after two attempts, which the packet already carries; no corpus source caps the intake itself.
One fact is already MUST-ask and never inferred - the Figma plan - and that class is the model a confidence model should borrow for the reader and the board's question.
